messages:
Ana (Billing): Heads up — customer Horizon Labs (PO PO-9987) flagged a proration/credit mismatch on INV-2026-0342 after a mid-cycle downgrade. They were billed for full month, downgraded on day 12 of 30, we issued a credit note but customer says refunded amount on their card != credit note total. :thinking:
Josh (Support): @Ana can you paste the invoice + credit note IDs and the refund transaction id? I can pull logs from the support side.
Ana (Billing): Credit note CN-2026-058, refund txn ref: r_1Jk9ZxZ. Customer says refund amount = 70.00 but CN shows 64.00 net + 6.00 VAT (we rounded differently).
Sarah (Finance): Quick theory: our credit notes are net-based (VAT as separate line) but payment gateway refund was processed on gross or vice-versa. That causes ledger mapping mismatch and customer-facing amount mismatch. Need to confirm tax handling on refund call. :eyes:
Keith (Payments): I pulled r_1Jk9ZxZ in Stripe: refund amount = 70.00 (currency USD), metadata shows "credit_note_id": "CN-2026-058" but tax_amount on refund object = 0. Looks like the refund call used the net amount only and Stripe recalculated? I'll paste raw: 
```
{"id":"r_1Jk9ZxZ","amount":7000,"currency":"usd","metadata":{"invoice":"INV-2026-0342","credit_note":"CN-2026-058"},"reason":"requested_by_customer","status":"succeeded"}
```
Marta (Sales): Customer is upset — they see $70 refunded on bank statement but credit note shows different breakdown, and their procurement team requires CN to match refund for PO reconciliation. Can we get a matching gross credit note?
Ana (Billing): Repro steps I used: 1) original plan $150/mo, downgrade to $50/mo on day 12 (30-day cycle). 2) prorated credit = (150-50) * (remaining_days/days_in_cycle) = 100 * 18/30 = 60. VAT 10% -> 6. Total gross credit = 66 but rounding/edgecases produced 64 net + 6 VAT in CN (we computed days differently). Customer shows 70 refund — not matching either.
Josh (Support): Are we double-applying taxes somewhere? Also did payments team issue any processing fees deducted?
Keith (Payments): No fee deducted on refund. The 70.00 on customer's statement is what Stripe returned. Possible causes: currency rounding, time-of-charge VAT rate, or we refunded original invoice gross (includes an earlier prorated add-on). I'll run full invoice/refund diff.
Sarah (Finance): For immediate mitigation: issue manual credit note that equals gross refund amount and link to original invoice and refund txn (CN-GROSS-2026-xxx). This keeps PO reconciliation intact. Then we'll reconcile journals to move the difference between net/vat buckets.
Ana (Billing): Agreed. I'll create manual CN and route for approval. Also adding repro SQL to find similar cases:
```
SELECT id, customer_id, amount_due, tax_amount, credit_note_id, refund_txn FROM invoices
WHERE customer_id = 'cust_horizon' AND period_start >= '2026-01-01';
```
Marta (Sales): Please cc me when you create the CN, I need to send to their procurement.
invoice-bot: Automated: CN-CHECK finished for CN-2026-058 — tax discrepancy flagged: expected_gross=70.00, recorded_gross=66.00.
Josh (Support): I'll follow up with the customer with an ETA and explain we're issuing a manual CN that matches bank refund. Keep thread posted with CN id and journal entry ids. :thumbsup:
Keith (Payments): I'll also add a guard in refunds flow to validate refund_amount == credit_note_gross when credit_note_id present and flag if mismatch (ticketed).
Sarah (Finance): Filing a short postmortem ticket for rounding/tax rules on proration -> assigning to Billing + Payments -> will include test cases for 28/29/30/31 day cycles and EU VAT variations.
Ana (Billing): Thanks — creating manual CN now and will drop CN id here when done.
